record.original_question: Let S be a finite simple nonabelian group that is not isomorphic to any group 2B2(q). A nonidentity automorphism x of S is called a τ-automorphism if every two conjugates of x in ⟨x, Inn(S)⟩ generate a subgroup of order not divisible by 3. If S admits a τ-automorphism, we call S a τ-group. (a) List all τ-groups up to isomorphism. (b) Do τ-automorphisms of odd order exist?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a finite nonabelian simple group that is not isomorphic to any Suzuki group ${}^2B_2(q)$. Identify $S$ with its inner automorphism group $\mathrm{Inn}(S)$ inside $\mathrm{Aut}(S)$. A nonidentity automorphism $x \in \mathrm{Aut}(S)$ is called a $\tau$-automorphism of $S$ if for every two conjugates $x_1, x_2$ of $x$ in the subgroup $\langle x, \mathrm{Inn}(S)\rangle \le \mathrm{Aut}(S)$, the order of the subgroup $\langle x_1, x_2\rangle$ is not divisible by $3$. A finite nonabelian simple group $S$ (not isomorphic to any ${}^2B_2(q)$) is called a $\tau$-group if it admits at least one $\tau$-automorphism.

(a) Determine, up to isomorphism, all $\tau$-groups.

(b) Decide whether there exists a $\tau$-automorphism of odd order (of any $\tau$-group).
